P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Partly established. Tajikistan has accepted IMF Article VIII (current-account convertibility). Dollar liquidity in banks is limited and can delay transactions. Residents must notify the National Bank of capital-movement FX operations and of opening foreign bank accounts (Instruction No. 223; not captured). No surrender requirement for service income was found.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Anyone earning on a regular basis must register as an individual entrepreneur (соҳибкори инфиродӣ) with the local tax authority, through the one-stop or single-window service, in person or online, and pay a registration fee. Documents: passport/ID and photos, and for foreigners a document authorising their stay (visa, registration card or residence permit). Patent-regime applicants prepay the first month's patent. Operating without registration doubles the tax rates.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents, meaning citizens and foreigners present more than 182 days in a consecutive 12-month period, are taxed on worldwide income. Non-registered individuals pay 15% on other income with no deductions (salary at the main workplace: 12%). Individual entrepreneurs choose a patent regime (fixed tax), a certificate regime or a certificate regime with special conditions. Deel reports that most pay a flat 6% of gross turnover under the simplified regime (Tax Code art. 380), while some sectors pay 13–20%.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Under the Tax Code (Art. 245), a person whose total income over a period of up to 12 consecutive full calendar months exceeds TJS 1.0 million becomes a VAT payer. Foreign entities performing remote services are also VAT payers. The standard rate is 14% for 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2026 and 13% from 1 January 2027 (Art. 397(4)). Smaller entrepreneurs (income under TJS 1 million) are 'small entrepreneurial activity'.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
